role: Commercial lawyer at a mid-sized firm in Beijing. I review and draft contracts, mostly supply and licensing agreements, in Chinese and English.
tasks: Reviewing counterparty redlines, drafting first versions of agreements from our precedents, and writing short advice notes for clients.
tools: Word with tracked changes, Outlook, PDF scans, Excel for fee estimates, and a document management system.
slow: Comparing a counterparty's redline against our standard position and writing up every deviation takes an entire afternoon.
tried: I asked a chatbot to summarise a 40-page agreement. It was fluent but it invented a clause number, so I stopped trusting it.
worries: Confidentiality above all. I cannot paste client documents into a public tool. Also accuracy: a wrong clause reference is a real problem.
goal: Turn a redline review into a checked deviation table in under an hour, and draft an advice note that I only need to edit rather than write.
